transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-16
Start: 14:30 PT
Duration: 1h14m
Attendees: Olivia (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Jinsoo (Redwood SE), Dr. Leah (Veridian ML), Arjun (Veridian Infra), Marta (Veridian PM), Simon (Veridian Security)

Summary:
Quick scoping workshop to align on how we'll measure POC success for latency and throughput SLOs. Primary focus: define measurement design for TTFT (time to first token) vs TPOT (tokens per total - per token throughput), decide p95/p99 targets, sampling methodology (logs vs synthetic replay), and assign stakeholder roles for running benchmarks and securing data. Veridian emphasizes compliance (PHI consideration) and private deployment constraints.

Topics discussed:
- Definition & importance of TTFT vs TPOT for chat UX and cost
- Percentile targets (p95/p99) and per-case SLO tiers (interactive vs batch)
- Workload sizing: traffic profile, payload length distribution, concurrency shaping
- Measurement plan: sampling size, warm vs cold cache, steady-state vs spike testing
- Roles & handoff: who runs harness, who supplies logs, security checklist items

Action items (recap at end): see metadata above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Olivia (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll do a 2 minute frame / goal. today we want to lock down how we'll measure POC success for latency and throughput — specifically TTFT vs TPOT — and who does what. quick intro, then Marcus will walk through a proposed benchmark design.

[00:22] Marcus (Redwood SE): thanks olivia. hi team. real quick definitions — i know you all have seen the terms, but TTFT we mean time to first token, that user-visible first byte delay. TPOT we're using as "per token steady-state throughput" or sometimes per-token processing time, so effectively how many ms per token under load, or tokens/sec depending on reporting. small note: we sometimes say tpot as taps, sorry verbal slip.

[00:48] Dr. Leah (ML Lead): sounds good. for Veridian, the patient-chat flows are the primary UX. TTFT is critical for clinician adoption. if first token is slow it's perceived as unusable.

[00:58] Marta (PM): yes, and we have two classes — short prompts (1-2 turns, ~50 tokens) and long context summaries (~800-2k tokens). the SLOs should probably be tiered.

[01:20] Marcus: exactly. our suggestion: classify into interactive (<=128 tokens) and longgeneration (>128 tokens). propose initial targets (draft): for interactive: TTFT p95 < 300ms, p99 < 600ms. TPOT p95 < 60ms/token, p99 < 150ms/token. for longgeneration we measure TTFT p95 < 800ms, p99 < 1.6s and TPOT measured at tokens/sec instead — goal ~15-30 tokens/sec dependent on quantization. these are starting points, obviously adjustable.

[02:05] Arjun (Infra): those numbers are... optimistic. what's underlying assumptions — hosted vs private infra? vm types? cache warm?

[02:15] Marcus: good call. baseline assumptions: 8k context model on A100 equivalent in dedicated pool, kv cache warm for multi-turn, and traffic shaped to match your concurrency. we'll run both warm-cache and cold-cache sweeps. that's why measurement plan matters.

[02:37] Jinsoo (Redwood SE): and we will provide kernel-level breakdowns in the telemetry so you can see time spent on token generation vs upload/serialization vs network egress. note some of the names may show up wrong in auto transcript, e.g., "KV cash" haha.

[02:50] Simon (Security): quick flag — Veridian handles PHI so we need the private deployment path. logs that we share must be HIPAA-safe and anonymized. also need KMS integration and audit logs from the get-go.

[03:10] Olivia: yep, security is in scope. next steps will include our security questionnaire and the SOC2 artifacts.

[03:22] Dr. Leah: about measurement — i'd prefer replay of real request logs rather than purely synthetic. synthetic can miss tail cases. we'll also want stratified sampling to ensure long-context samples are represented.

[03:38] Marcus: agreed. plan: customer provides 7 days of request logs (anonymized) — we will extract sample population and create stratified buckets by token-length, model path (chat vs completion), and concurrency. recommended sample sizes: min 1,000 requests per bucket for steady-state p95/p99 estimation, though for p99 more samples better — aim for 5k when feasible.

[04:12] Marta: 5k per bucket could be heavy; do you have guidance on run time? like how long will a run take?

[04:20] Marcus: depends on concurrency. example: with a 50-concurrency load we can simulate a day of traffic in a few hours. we'll also provide a harness so your infra team can run locally in VPC. we'll coordinate to avoid production impact.

[04:39] Arjun: local run is key. we need a runbook for how to allocate test nodes and where to mount KMS; and also how to do warm-up so cache can be primed deterministically.

[04:52] Jinsoo: runbook we promise — includes warm/cold cache procedure: 1) cold-run (no kv priming) 2) controlled priming stage (replay 10% of traffic) 3) steady-state measurement 4) spike step-up tests. we'll include scripts to measure TTFT (client observed) and per-token timers inside the runtime.

[05:20] Dr. Leah: on the SLOs: p95 is great but we care about p99 too because our clinicians will hit edge cases. curious how we account for network jitter vs model time.

[05:34] Marcus: we'll capture breakdowns. recommended acceptance criteria will separate client-network latency (measured at client runner) and server-side processing. final SLOs will be server-side TTFT p95/p99 thresholds plus an overall end-to-end budget. e.g., server-side TTFT p95 <= 240ms leaving 60ms for network to hit a 300ms user-facing p95.

[06:05] Marta: OK, so two buckets: server-only and end-to-end. track both in the report.

[06:12] Olivia: yes. another consideration: model variants and fallback. if we need graceful degradation, we'll define failover performance and acceptable degradation bands as part of the acceptance matrix.

[06:26] Arjun: i want to make sure we measure contention — multiple tenants / shared GPUs? but for POC we'll use a dedicated pool right?

[06:34] Marcus: for consistency we'll use dedicated reserved capacity for the benchmark. we can also run stress tests against a shared pool to show difference.

[06:45] Simon: logging & audit — please confirm we can get request-level traces with pseudonymized IDs for correlation to our internal logs.

[06:55] Jinsoo: yes, we'll produce traces and an event CSV that aligns with your anonymized request IDs. policy: we won't retain raw payloads beyond the bench window unless you opt-in.

[07:12] Dr. Leah: measurement granularity — how do you recommend calculating p99 reliably? i've seen unstable p99 with small sample sizes.

[07:22] Marcus: we recommend multiple independent runs (3-5) and aggregate using medians of percentiles or compute bootstrap confidence intervals. for p99 we prefer either larger sample sizes or using the block maxima approach. details will be in the measurement plan doc.

[07:40] Olivia: let's talk timelines: if you provide logs by 9/22 we can produce an initial sampling and harness by 9/23, run baseline bench by 9/25, and share results 9/26. does that work?

[07:54] Marta: that is aggressive but ok. need internal approval but looks doable.

[08:02] Arjun: depends on whether we need an on-prem appliance for the private test. that could add a week.

[08:10] Marcus: note: our private deployment quick-start can be deployed to a test VPC in 48-72 hours if infra prerequisites are met.

[08:20] Dr. Leah: one more: for long generation we should record tokens/sec as aggregate and per-step token timing to catch tail effects when attention grows.

[08:32] Jinsoo: yep, for long context we capture per-token timing and memory stall metrics. we'll include probe for attention compute spikes.

[08:42] Olivia: ok wrapping — recap of what we committed: 1) Marcus to build harness + sampling script, 2) Veridian to send logs + allocate test VPC, 3) Olivia to send legal/security package and pilot pricing, 4) schedule runbook session.

[08:58] Marcus: and measurement doc will specify warm/cold definitions, sample sizes (min 1k-5k), bucket stratification, run repeat counts, and p95/p99 aggregation method.

[09:12] Marta: good. can you also include instructions to capture failed requests and their effect on percentiles? we need transparency around error budgets.

[09:24] Jinsoo: yes we will mark and report errors separately and include fallback routing logs.

[09:32] Olivia: great. i'll follow up with calendar invites for the workshop and the runbook walkthrough. thanks everyone.

[09:38] Meeting end.
